$comment: England & Wales, Landlord & Tenant Law - Housing Act 1988 s.21 'no-fault' possession and Trecarrell House v Rouncefield's gas-safety-record timing point. IMPORTANT: s.21 (Housing Act 1988, Part I Chapter 2) was omitted from 1 May 2026 by the Renters' Rights Act 2025, discovered live during this session's research rather than assumed from training data - as of this file's verified_at date, s.21 is HISTORICAL/TRANSITIONAL doctrine, not current operative practice for new notices. Possession now requires the s.8 statutory-grounds route. This entry is retained because a substantial volume of pre-1 May 2026 notices were still working through the courts as the transitional deadline (31 July 2026, for issuing proceedings on a pre-commencement notice) had only just passed as of this file's verification date - not because s.21 describes current practice going forward.
verification_method: Housing Act 1988 s.21 fetched live and directly from legislation.gov.uk, including its live status banner showing the Renters' Rights Act 2025 repeal. Trecarrell House Ltd v Rouncefield [2020] EWCA Civ 760 fetched live and directly from Find Case Law, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time (case name, citation, court, date, panel, split-decision outcome, and the para 30 quote) before being relied on here.

authorities.name: Housing Act 1988, s.21 (Chapter 2, Part I) - 'no-fault' accelerated possession
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. THIS PROVISION IS NO LONGER GENERALLY OPERATIVE - Part I Chapter 2 (containing s.21) was omitted with effect from 1 May 2026 by the Renters' Rights Act 2025, confirmed live via legislation.gov.uk's own status banner this session. Transitional savings allowed a landlord to serve a pre-commencement notice up to 28 April 2026 and issue possession proceedings on it up to 31 July 2026 - both dates have now passed as of this file's verification date.
authorities.proposition: As it stood in force before 1 May 2026: on the ending of a fixed-term assured shorthold tenancy, a court had to make a possession order if the tenancy had ended with no further assured tenancy in existence (other than a periodic shorthold), and the landlord had given the tenant at least two months' written notice requiring possession - a mechanism requiring no fault or ground to be shown. Recorded here as historical/transitional doctrine only, not current operative practice - see the caveat above.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, including the live status banner confirming omission by the Renters' Rights Act 2025. 'treatment: OVERRULED' is used here in the sense of 'legislatively superseded/repealed', not a court overruling - schemas/authority.schema.json's treatment enum has no dedicated 'REPEALED' value, and OVERRULED is the closest accurate fit for 'no longer good law' rather than mischaracterising it as GOOD_LAW_CURRENT.

authorities.name: Trecarrell House Ltd v Rouncefield
authorities.judge_or_panel: Patten LJ and King LJ (majority); Moylan LJ (dissenting)
authorities.proposition: A landlord's failure to give the tenant a Gas Safety Record before the tenant went into occupation (a breach of the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998, reg.36(6)/(7)) does not permanently bar use of the s.21 procedure - the majority (Patten LJ, King LJ) held that late delivery of the record, provided before the s.21 notice itself is served, cures the earlier breach for s.21 purposes. Moylan LJ dissented, considering the failure to provide the record before occupation began to be irremediable and to bar a s.21 claim permanently. Supreme Court permission to appeal further was refused, making this the settled Court of Appeal authority on the point for the period s.21 remained in force.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, and independently re-fetched a second time to confirm the split-decision outcome and the para 30 majority reasoning before being relied on here. Relevant only to notices served, and possession proceedings issued, before s.21's repeal took effect - see AUTH-EW-LT-001's caveat.

edges.verified_via: Trecarrell House Ltd v Rouncefield [2020] EWCA Civ 760, para 30 (Patten LJ), fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: construes the timing requirement for gas-safety compliance under the now-repealed s.21 procedure.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes, both now historical/transitional following s.21's repeal from 1 May 2026 - retained for matters still working through the courts on pre-commencement notices, not as current operative practice. Does not cover the s.8 statutory-grounds possession route that has replaced s.21 for new cases, the Renters' Rights Act 2025's own substantive reforms, the landlord's repairing obligations (Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 s.11), rent increases, deposit protection, or any other Landlord & Tenant subject - all remain unbuilt. Anyone using this file for a live 2026-or-later matter must confirm the s.8/Renters' Rights Act 2025 framework applies instead, not assume s.21 is available.
